purpose: Adds image_editor cache group awareness to the Redis Object Cache drop-in, with flush_group() support for WP 6.7's new image_editor cache group.
riskRationale: The implementation is generally correct and follows existing patterns, but has a WP version compatibility gap (wp_cache_supports('flush_group') not registered for WP < 6.7) and unnecessarily clears the entire local cache on group flush.

text: The PR correctly implements the three changes described: registering image_editor as a global group, adding flush_group() to WP_Object_Cache, and adding the wp_cache_flush_group() wrapper. The SCAN/DEL pattern correctly mirrors the existing flush() logic with proper RedisCluster support. However, two issues need attention: (1) the drop-in doesn't register flush_group with wp_cache_supports(), breaking consumer code in class-cache.php on WP < 6.7, and (2) flush_group() over-aggressively clears all local cache entries instead of only the targeted group's.

reasoning: The implementation matches the PR description, but has a WP version compatibility gap and an unnecessarily aggressive local cache clear. Both are straightforward fixes.

message: SCAN/DEL implementation correctly mirrors the existing flush() pattern, including proper RedisCluster _masters() iteration and the same cursor loop logic. This ensures consistency and reduces cognitive overhead for maintainers.
The wp_cache_flush_group() wrapper follows the exact same convention as all other global cache functions in the file, making it immediately recognizable to anyone familiar with the codebase.
Registering image_editor as a global group is the right call — image editor data is server-wide, not site-specific, so blog-prefixed keys would cause redundant cache entries on multisite.

flush_group() clears the entire local cache ($this->cache = array()) instead of only entries belonging to the targeted group. This causes unnecessary cache misses for unrelated groups after a targeted flush. The existing flush() method does the same, but flush() is a full flush so it's justified there; flush_group() has a narrower contract.
suggestion: Iterate over $this->cache and unset only keys matching the group prefix, rather than clearing the entire local cache array. Alternatively, document this as an intentional simplification if the performance cost is deemed acceptable.

message: The drop-in adds flush_group support but does not register it via wp_cache_supports(). Consumer code in class-cache.php::flush_group() checks wp_cache_supports('flush_group'), which returns false on WP < 6.7 (the plugin's minimum is 6.2). This means the entire feature path silently returns false on older WP versions, despite the drop-in actually supporting it.
suggestion: Remove the wp_cache_supports('flush_group') guard from class-cache.php::flush_group() — the function_exists('wp_cache_flush_group') and method_exists($wp_object_cache, 'flush_group') checks are sufficient guards on their own. The wp_cache_supports() check adds a false dependency on WP core awareness that the drop-in cannot influence without a more invasive change.
